notes: REPLACES AN AMOSTOOLS STUB. Until 2026-08-12 this row held only the token table with the library stripped out from under it -- both length fields zero, no code, every routine word overwritten with `====` -- so the tier could not rise above `manual`. The real library's table is IDENTICAL to the stub's, entry for entry, id for id and spec for spec, which is a check on the AMOSTools reader as much as on this registration. What changes is that the code is now here to read. THE LIBRARY IS CALLED `Tiny.lib` and nothing about that filename says which extension it is -- it was identified from its token table, which carries `opengui`, `closegui`, `wait`, `waitport`, `getimsg`, `replyimsg`, `gotoamos`, `gotowb`, this row's names exactly. 1,208 bytes, the smallest library registered. WHAT IT IS FOR, and it explains the odd keyword names: OrgAsm is a TRANSLATOR, not a GUI library. In the author's words it "'sits' between two other programs, namely GadToolsBox and A68k" -- you paint an interface in GadToolsBox, save it as assembler, and OrgAsm rewrites that source into something AMOS can use and assembles it into Ram:GUI.BIN and Ram:GUI.ASC. The extension is only the runtime that loads the resulting blob and pumps its message port, which is why fourteen keywords is enough and why they are spelled `f<opengui>` rather than `Open Gui`. The six example programs (1_Buttons through 6-TooMany, 6KB to 14KB) are the only demonstration of what the keywords do -- the readme documents the translator, not the runtime.
